stories.headline: Govt condemns vandalism of Indian embassy in Slovenia
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Condemning the defacement of Indian embassy premises in Slovenia by Khalistan separatists, the govt urged law enforcement authorities elsewhere too to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups.
Ministry of external affairs said in an official statement that under the Vienna Convention, diplomatic premises are inviolable and must be protected.
"We have taken up the matter strongly with Slovenian authorities, both in New Delhi and in Ljubljana so that the perpetrators behind such reprehensible acts are held accountable to the full extent of the law," it said.
"We also call upon law enforcement authorities elsewhere to take note of the hateful propaganda and disinformation being spread by such groups," it added.
In recent years, Indian diplomatic missions have been targeted, vandalised, or defaced with pro-Khalistan slogans and flags in many other countries, including Australia, Canada, UK and the US.

stories.headline: Six years after start of work, Varthur elevated corridor gets December 2026 deadline
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 After years of missed deadlines, Karnataka Road Development Corporation Ltd (KRDCL) has set Dec as the latest target for completing the long-delayed Rs 488-crore Varthur elevated corridor, raising hopes for commuters on one of the most congested stretches near Bengaluru’s tech corridor.
The revised deadline was announced at a review meeting Monday, where KRDCL managing director Susheelamma N and project officials directed the contractor to expedite pending works and complete the project by year-end.
The 100ft elevated corridor on SH-35, work on which began on May 20, 2019, was originally scheduled for completion by Nov 2021. Land acquisition, utility shifting, approvals, and execution delays have since pushed the project back repeatedly, leaving lakhs of commuters from Varthur, Gunjur and surrounding areas battling congestion and prolonged construction.
“Eighty per cent of the land acquisition is complete, and the delay appears to be largely on the contractor’s end. We’ll ensure the project is completed by year-end without fail,” said KRDCL managing director Susheelamma N.
KRDCL said it plans to hold a meeting with residents to hear their grievances and review the ongoing works on the ground. The agency has completed side-drain works and demolished more than 50 properties between Varthur Kodi and Varthur police station, but pending land acquisition and right-of-way issues continue to hamper progress.
Despite the latest assurance, residents remain sceptical after six years of missed deadlines.
Crumbling infrastructure
The SH-35 corridor connecting Whitefield, Varthur, Gunjur, Sarjapur, and Outer Ring Road has seen rapid residential and commercial growth, but infrastructure has failed to keep pace. Narrow carriageways, unfinished drains, damaged roads, and missing footpaths continue to trouble commuters. “The road is in a perpetual state of construction. During summer, dust enters homes and vehicles. During rain, potholes disappear under water, making commuting dangerous,” said a Varthur resident.
The corridor is also dotted with schools, hospitals and residential communities, with congestion frequently delaying school buses, emergency vehicles and public transport.
Citizen groups said they have submitted over 100 representations to KRDCL, Greater Bengaluru Authority, and elected representatives, seeking faster execution and a firm completion timeline. With the latest deadline set for Dec 2026, residents said they would judge the project by progress on the ground, not official assurances.
Land acquisition hurdle
According to data, 14 properties are yet to be acquired, with cases pending over Transferable Development Rights (TDR) or cash compensation. Several property owners are yet to consent to TDR or submit the required documents.
Authorities have indicated that land acquisition proceedings under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act-2013 may be initiated where TDR processing is not feasible. On the Varthur police station–Gunjur stretch, officials have also directed KRDCL to take possession of the road land required for drains so pending works can proceed without delay.
TOI reality check
A recent 
TOI
 visit to the Varthur-Gunjur stretch on a rainy afternoon revealed grim conditions. Commuters navigated cratered roads, waterlogged potholes and barricaded drain-work stretches, while debris from demolished structures narrowed the road further.
School buses, cars, two-wheelers and autos jostled for space, causing long queues. Pedestrians waited along narrow road edges amid moving traffic. Residents said the stretch becomes particularly hazardous during rain, when potholes are hard to spot and roads turn slushy.
What Residents Say
Monalisa Goswami, Varthur resident, said: “The corridor has seen rapid growth, but infrastructure has failed to keep pace. Residents continue to grapple with poor roads, missing footpaths, drainage problems and severe congestion. With multiple agencies involved, there is still little clarity on timelines or accountability. The question remains: who will take responsibility and finish the project?”
Sanjiv Sharma, another resident, said: “I think apartments were approved without ensuring existing infrastructure could handle the additional traffic. Even good roads may not solve the problem if development continues unchecked. Large projects near Dommasandra are due for occupancy soon, while more apartments in Gunjur are expected within a year. We are already suffering every day, and the situation could only worsen.”
Project TimelineMay 2019:
 KRDCL awards Varthur Elevated Corridor project
Nov 2021:
 Original completion deadline
2022-2025:
 Delays linked to land acquisition, right-of-way issues and approvals
2026:
 Multiple portions still pending; residents seek intervention and accountability
Dec 2026: New deadline to finish project
What Residents Want
* Public disclosure of current project status
* Time-bound completion schedule
* Monthly progress reports
* Single nodal officer for coordination
* Faster resolution of land acquisition issues
* Review of contractor performance
* Safe footpaths and proper drainage across the corridor
* Accountability for delays since 2019

stories.headline: Bengaluru techie ends life, accuses wife & family of harassment
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Allegedly harassed by his wife and her family, a newlywed techie died by suicide by hanging from a tree at Aratabele village in Kanakapura, Bengaluru South district, Sunday.
The victim Roshan Jameer, who worked with a private firm in Jayanagar, had married Ikra Fatima one month ago. But Fatima returned to her parents’ home a week after marriage, citing differences, police said. However, Jameer would continue to visit her regularly.
Jameer’s family alleged to police that Fatima’s parents had insulted him. When Jameer was in office, they entered his house and took away Fatima’s valuables. They also filed a false domestic violence case against Jameer at Basavanagudi women’s police station.
Police said Jameer left behind a message on his mobile, accusing Fatima, her parents and others of abetting his suicide through harassment. Based on a complaint filed by Jameer’s father Anwar Pasha, Kanakapura Rural police registered abetment-to-suicide case against Fatima and others.
If you are having suicidal thoughts or are in need of emotional support, call suicide-prevention helplines: Tele-Manas helpline: 14416 or 1800-891-4416, SAHAI Helpline: 080-25497777.

stories.headline: HCG profit nearly triples to Rs 16.5 cr in June quarter
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
Cancer hospital chain HealthCare Global Enterprises (HCG) nearly tripled its profit to Rs 16.5 crore in the June quarter from about Rs 6 crore a year ago, driven by higher patient volumes and capacity expansion.
Total income rose 14% year-on-year to Rs 707 crore, from Rs 620 crore in the year-ago quarter. Patient volumes increased 11%, while average revenue per patient grew 2%.
Growth was strongest in eastern India, where revenue rose 22%, followed by the south at 16%. The western region, HCG’s largest market by revenue, grew 9%.
HCG added 121 operational beds during the quarter as it expanded its cancer-care network. More than half of the new capacity came from its North Bengaluru hospital, which began operations in May with 56 beds. The facility recorded more than 550 new patient registrations and over 300 admissions in its first few weeks.
Sixteen of HCG’s 25 centres, excluding the newly opened North Bengaluru hospital, reported their highest-ever quarterly revenue. Revenue from cash-paying and insured patients also increased during the quarter.
The company is gearing up for a larger expansion, with plans to add around 1,000 beds by FY30. About 60% of the new capacity is expected to come from expanding existing hospitals rather than setting up entirely new facilities.

stories.headline: I am also out on bail, says Shivakumar as he defends Nagendra’s inclusion in cabinet
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Newly inducted minister B Nagendra, whose return to the cabinet has triggered sharp criticism from 
BJP
 and discontent among some Congress MLAs who were denied ministerial berths, received a double reprieve on Monday, with chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 strongly defending his re-induction and the high court relaxing a key bail condition imposed on him in the Maharshi Valmiki Development Corporation case.
The high court stayed the condition requiring Nagendra to seek the court’s permission before travelling outside Karnataka. It modified the condition to allow him to travel within the country, while retaining the requirement to obtain court permission before leaving India. The court gave the Enforcement Directorate (ED) time till Wednesday to file objections. Nagendra had approached the high court after the special court for elected representatives rejected his plea to travel to Delhi.
The legal relief comes as BJP and JD(S) prepare to jointly pile pressure on Shivakumar to drop Nagendra from his council of ministers over allegations linked to the transfer of Rs 187 crore from the corporation. Nagendra had resigned as Scheduled Tribe welfare minister from the Siddaramaiah cabinet in 2024 after the alleged irregularities came to light and is currently out on bail.
Defending his re-induction on Sunday, Shivakumar said being an accused and being out on bail did not automatically disqualify a person from being a minister.
“I am also on bail. Didn’t HD Kumaraswamy obtain bail? There are many ministers in the country who are on bail,” Shivakumar said, adding that it was the right of the opposition to raise the issue.
However, opposition leader R Ashoka renewed BJP’s attack Monday, calling Nagendra “tainted” and alleging that he had travelled to New Delhi in violation of a court order.
Ashoka said investigations by agencies including CBI and ED were still underway and questioned the decision to bring Nagendra back into the cabinet. “If a tainted MLA is re-inducted into cabinet, then, the entire cabinet will be tainted,” Ashoka said.
State BJP president BY Vijayendra alleged Nagendra had “blackmailed” the CM and Congress high command, claiming party brass was also aware of the alleged threats. “We have information that Nagendra even blackmailed the Congress high command. The issue of threats being made is also being discussed within Congress circles,” Vijayendra alleged adding that his induction into the cabinet amounted to an “injustice” to the Scheduled Tribe community.

stories.headline: Contradicting BJP, Horatti says he was not forced to resign
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Turning accusations by BJP and JD(S) on their head, Basavaraj Horatti clarified Monday that he was not forced to resign as legislative council chairman and that chief minister DK Shivakumar did not pressure him to go but wanted him to quit earlier than the date he had decided on.
Horatti’s account comes amid a political row over his resignation ahead of the monsoon session of the legislature, with BJP-JD(S) accusing the govt of threatening Horatti “like goondas” to engineer the exit of the eight-time MLC and Shivakumar alleging that the opposition was attempting to manufacture a constitutional crisis.
Horatti told TOI that he had decided to resign on Friday (Aug 14), but Shivakumar and his team urged him to do so immediately. “When the CM himself says it, what can one do? Considering that I had to resign someday, I decided to quit immediately,” Horatti said.
The former chairman said he subsequently submitted a letter to Shivakumar stating that he had resigned on Aug 7 and that the communication had reached the CM.
Horatti also clarified that he does not intend to turn the issue into a personal confrontation with the govt. He said he would not raise the matter on his own in the House but would explain what happened if the issue is brought up by others.
“I will narrate the entire sequence of events and what transpired over the past few days,” he said.
The resignation has nevertheless given BJP-JD(S) an opportunity to target the govt over the way in which a veteran legislator was made to quit office.
Meanwhile, speaking in New Delhi on the issue late Monday night, Shivakumar rejected BJP-JD(S) allegations, insisting Horatti’s resignation had been properly submitted and accepted.
“BJP-JD(S) are trying to create a constitutional crisis by lodging this complaint (with the governor),” Shivakumar said. “I feel sorry for the senior legislator who is being used as a scapegoat by BJP. We apprised the governor of the legal points in the matter and pointed out that the resignation was given to the office. It has been accepted as well, so there is no illegality.”
The immediate political consequence is likely to be the election of a new council chairman on Friday, Congress functionaries say. Thursday, the first day of the monsoon session, is likely to be dominated by condolences for those who have died since the legislature last met.

stories.headline: West Asia war fallout: Oil product exports find many new markets
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: The West Asia crisis has opened several new markets for India’s oil product exports, with Italy and Spain among those at the top of growth charts, while Singapore and Tanzania have zoomed past traditional destinations.
Propelled by oil, Singapore has emerged as the third largest goods export destination for India, while Tanzania and South Africa have broken into top 10, according to disaggregated data for the first quarter. Among countries with close to a $1 billion of imports from India, govt data showed that the highest growth was in countries, such as Tanzania, Jordan and Sri Lanka (See graphic). Of course, higher prices have also had a role to play in value of exports rising.
In almost all cases – barring Hong Kong and Vietnam – the rise in exports was driven by oil product shipments, with countries relying on Indian refineries to meet their requirements, amid supply disruptions. In fact, since the war started in West Asia, govt had to impose windfall tax on certain products to keep a check on outward movement.
Since the war started in West Asia, govt had to impose windfall tax on certain products to keep a check on outward movement.
As a result, the share of oil products in the exports to these countries has gone up significantly. 
For instance, the share of oil products in India’s exports to Tanzania has increased to 77% at the end of the June quarter, compared with 59% a year ago, while it has doubled to 32% in the case of Sri Lanka. Two-thirds of exports to Singapore – the largest destination for export of India refined petroleum products – are now accounted for by refined goods - against 40% during April-June 2025.
For countries such as Spain and France, now share of oil products is around 15%, compared to nearly zero last year.
When it comes to growth rates too, Spain is near the top, with the value of oil product shipments zooming from $4 million in the first quarter of the last fiscal year to $252 million this year – a 63-fold jump. Italy is on top, with exports soaring from $2 million to $478 million, official data showed. And when it comes to the top destinations, Singapore overtook the Netherlands, UAE, the US and Australia, with the value of oil product exports pegged at $4.3 billion, followed by Tanzania ($2.2 billion) and the Netherlands ($2billion) despite a 41% decline.

stories.headline: SpaceX retail investors turn net sellers for first time since IPO; offload $4.5 million worth of shares
stories.deck: Retail investors turned into net sellers of SpaceX shares as of August 7, marking the end of a buying frenzy. This change coincided with a stock price recovery, indicating that individuals may be taking profits. The shares have struggled post-IPO, dropping beneath the initial offering price. Investors who were hopeful at the launch might now be looking to reduce their losses, even amidst a slight…
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Retail investors turned net sellers of 
SpaceX
 shares on August 7, marking the first such instance since the company's blockbuster public debut in June, according to Vanda Research.
Individual investors sold a net $4.5 million worth of SpaceX shares on the day, reported Reuters. The shift came after a period of strong retail buying, including a major dip-buying spree following a 13.6 per cent fall in the stock on August 5.
“A shift from persistent net buying to selling is rarely about one catalyst, it is usually a mix of profit-taking, position fatigue and investors reassessing the risk-reward,” said Sam North, market analyst at eToro.
“Friday is particularly interesting because retail turned net sellers while the shares were rebounding strongly and trading back around the IPO price. That looks more like investors using strength to take some money off the table than panic selling,” North said, as quoted by Reuters.
SpaceX shares have struggled after an early post-IPO rally. The stock had climbed as much as 67 per cent above its $135 IPO price in June before giving up those gains and falling more than 22 per cent below the debut price in August. 
Shares were last up 1.4 per cent at $134.95 in early trading on Monday, after gaining nearly 23 per cent last week.
Despite the recent recovery, the stock has closed below its $135 IPO price every day since July 16.
Retail investors have played a significant role in SpaceX's public-market debut, with at least 30% of the shares offered at launch reserved for retail buyers. Jai Malhi, senior equities strategist at Vanda, estimated that retail traders paid an average of $147 for SpaceX shares since the IPO, suggesting that “the selling may have been a function of cutting losses at an opportune time.”
Retail interest in the stock remains high. SpaceX was the second-most mentioned ticker on Reddit forum r/WallStreetBets over the past week, according to sentiment aggregator SwaggyStocks.
The latest shift also comes as the number of SpaceX shares available for public trading more than doubled after the expiry of the first of several lock-up restrictions last week.

stories.headline: TRAI directs use of 1601-series for service, transactional calls by utilities, logistics cos
stories.deck: At present, the 1600-series numbers are allotted for service and transactional calls by the BFSI sector and Government entities.
stories.bodyText:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) on Monday (August 10, 2026) directed the use of a separate 1601-series number for transactional and service calls by entities in sectors other than Banking, Financial Services & Insurance (BFSI) and Government.
In the first phase, the 1601 number series will cover transactional and service calls made by entities in utilities, courier and logistics sectors, TRAI said, making it clear that such dedicated number series should not be used for promotional voice calls by any entity.
At present, the 1600-series numbers are allotted for service and transactional calls by the BFSI sector and Government entities.
The telecom regulator said that considering the critical and sensitive nature of communications made by the entities in the BFSI sector and Government, a separate series of 1601 has been issued for other sectors in order to avoid mixing of important financial voice calls with the service and transactional calls from the other sectors.
“After widespread adoption of the 1600-series numbers for service and transactional calls by BFSI sector entities, which has provided valuable experience for extending the trusted numbering framework to the other sectors also, TRAI has now initiated phase-wise implementation of the 1601-series allotted by the DoT (Department of Telecom) for similar calls by the entities in sectors other than the BFSI sector and Government,” TRAI said.
According to the regulator, based on consultations with stakeholders, it has been decided to implement 1601-series, covering entities in utilities, courier and logistics sectors under Phase-I.
The 1601-series numbers will be allocated directly to eligible entities, and not to intermediaries or aggregators, after due verification by the telecom service providers (TSPs).
Their adoption is, therefore, expected to become an important tool in combating impersonation by fraudsters who use normal 10-digit numbers and falsely claim to represent legitimate businesses, TRAI said.
Moreover, the distinct numbering identity will enable consumers to easily identify legitimate service and transactional calls, thereby strengthening trust in such voice-based communications, as per TRAI.
Accordingly, the 1601-series shall be initially allocated to the eligible entities in the utilities and logistics and courier services space. The category of utilities entails electricity distribution companies, water utilities, city gas distribution companies, LPG distribution entities and similar other utility service providers.
The logistics and courier services companies would include courier firms, express logistics companies, parcel delivery service providers, as well as freight and logistics service providers engaged in delivery of consignments.
The telecom operators have been asked to complete migration and on-boarding of eligible entities covered under the first phase within 90 days.
"The TSPs shall verify the eligibility of entities before assigning 1601-series numbers, and obtain an undertaking from them regarding exclusive use of these numbers for service and transactional voice calls," TRAI said.
It is pertinent to mention that while TRAI mandated the use of 1600 series numbers for service and transaction calls by regulated banking, financial services and insurance or BFSI entities, and government-to-citizen communications, the 140 series numbers are for promotional calls by registered entities across sectors.
Last month, there was a standoff between TRAI and Truecaller over the display of tags on dedicated 140 and 1600 number series. Truecaller alleged that spam calls have surged after TRAI mandated the use of dedicated 140 and 1600 number series while preventing caller ID apps from displaying community-reported spam information for those numbers.
The regulator hit back, saying Truecaller should display a label informing users that they can "exercise their choice" to block unwanted communication from the 140 series through TRAI's official Do Not Disturb (DND) preference management app.
TRAI has repeatedly cautioned call management apps and users that under no circumstances should the 1600 number be tagged as such, given that this series is used for service and transaction calls by regulated entities of the BFSI sector (entities regulated by RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA) to their existing customers and by government entities for government-to-citizen communication.
What this implies is calls from the 1600 series could range from fraud alerts to transaction verification, and tagging or labelling them in any form may have adverse consequences for consumers.
According to a recent TRAI report, as many as 1.15 billion calls originated from 1600 dedicated series numbers during Q1 FY2026-27.
Published - August 10, 2026 09:59 pm IST

stories.headline: Geopolitics drives valuation discipline for IPOs in H1-2026
stories.deck: Companies, which may have planned to list in the beginning of the calendar year, deferred their plans, as geopolitical tensions made stock markets volatile and outcomes of listing uncertain.
stories.bodyText:
Valuations of companies planning to get listed on the stock markets have moderated to more “disciplined” levels, following increased market volatility driven by geopolitical uncertainties.
“Investors are rewarding companies with strong fundamentals. Clear earnings visibility and reasonable valuations continue to receive strong demand, while aggressively priced initial public offerings (IPOs) are seeing a more cautious response,” said Sumeet Lath, Associate Director and Co-Head - ECM Execution at Anand Rathi Advisors Limited.
This was not the case last year when several issuers sought to maximise valuations by pricing their IPOs at the upper end of listed peer multiples, he added.
Companies that seek listing have adjusted to this reality. Many of the entities, which may have planned to list in the beginning of the calendar year, deferred their plans, as geopolitical tensions made stock markets volatile and outcomes of listing uncertain.
“This is working well for investors too. IPOs with market capitalisation between ₹8000 crore to ₹40,000 crore is a sweet spot for investments as this falls under multiple investment manadates” said Bharat Lahoti, President and co-head, Factor investing, Edelweiss Mutual Fund.
There is also a growing race against time to complete the listing, as favourable issuance windows are becoming fewer and less predictable, especially with the expiry of the listing application looming, according to Lath.
“As of June 2026, 176 companies had valid Securities and Exchange Bpard of India (SEBI) approvals, while 74 more were awaiting approval, with many aiming to tap the market during the September–October window,” he said.
An IPO is typically a 3–4 year journey, with SEBI approval being the final milestone, after which the company has a one-year window to launch.
Several companies therefore choose to proceed despite lower-than-desired valuations or reduced issue size, rather than wait for ideal market conditions and risk letting their approval lapse, said Pranav Haldea, MD of PRIME Database.
A slower IPO market has led to the beginning of the next cycle. This transition period of pricing discipline is the beginning of the next IPO boom, Mr. Lahoti concluded.
Published - August 10, 2026 08:26 pm IST

stories.headline: Ethanol or EVs? India needs both for cleaner mobility, says IFGE
stories.bodyText:
India's shift towards cleaner mobility will require multiple technologies rather than a choice between ethanol and 
electric vehicles
, the Indian Federation of Green Energy (IFGE) said, pointing to the continued presence of nearly 300 million internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles on the country's roads.
The federation said that ethanol, electric vehicles, hybrids, CNG and hydrogen should form part of a diversified energy strategy. Its comments come amid concerns about the effect of E20 petrol on vehicle mileage and compatibility.
"The debate should not be framed as ethanol versus EVs India needs both. E20 provides an immediate pathway to reduce crude oil dependence and strengthen energy security, while EVs, hybrids and other technologies continue to scale," said Dilip Patil, Regional Director, IFGE-West, Pune.
IFGE said the reduction in fuel efficiency associated with E20 has been estimated at 2-6 per cent compared with E10, citing studies by the Automotive Research Association of India (ARAI), Indian Oil and the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM).
At the same time, the industry body said testing has not indicated widespread engine damage. It added that newer vehicles are increasingly using ethanol-compatible materials, while concerns are largely linked to the transition involving older vehicles.
India completed nationwide E20 deployment by April 2025 and is now expanding higher ethanol blends, flex-fuel vehicles and second-generation ethanol, according to IFGE.
The ethanol blending programme has also helped reduce the country's reliance on imported crude. The latest figures released by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas show that the programme has generated foreign-exchange savings of more than Rs 1.97 lakh crore and substituted nearly 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil since Ethanol Supply Year 2014-15.
The government has been promoting ethanol blending as part of its efforts to cut dependence on imported crude oil and increase the use of domestically produced fuels.

stories.headline: Praggnanandhaa to meet Samuel in first round of Sinquefield Cup
stories.deck: Samuel Sevian is a surprise entry in the Sinquefield Cup, after French Grandmaster Alireza Firouzja decided to withdraw from the tour
stories.bodyText:
In high spirits after his victory in the St. Louis Rapid and Blitz, which elevated him to second place in the overall Grand Chess Tour rankings, R. Praggnanandhaa, barring a debacle here, is likely to feature in the finale later this year.
The Grand Chess Tour (GCT) Finals are contested by the top-four finishers on the tour, and currently, American Grandmaster Fabiano Caruana is ahead of Praggnanandhaa.
Samuel Sevian is a surprise entry in the Sinquefield Cup, after French Grandmaster Alireza Firouzja decided to withdraw from the tour.
All nine regular tour players will be back in the Sinquefield Cup, making it one of the strongest tournaments of the year, alongside the Norway Chess Classic, which was also won by Praggnanandhaa.
Caruana starts as the favourite yet again, as classical chess is his forte, while fellow Americans, Wesley So and Levon Aronian, will also be among the contenders for a podium finish.
Add to that, World Championship contender Javokhir Sindarov of Uzbekistan, Vincent Keymer of Germany, Anish Giri of the Netherlands and Maxime Vachier-Lagrave of France, and it becomes an extremely formidable field.
The other player is Jorden van Foreest of the Netherlands, who, on his day, can make anyone bite the dust.
The tournament will be played over nine rounds between 10 players on a round-robin basis, with a total prize pool of $475,000.
In the recently concluded St. Louis Rapid and Blitz, Praggnanandhaa, who turned 21 on Monday, won by a 1.5-point margin over Sindarov, and the Indian can certainly hope for an encore given his superior recent form.
Praggnanandhaa will have five Black games out of a possible nine and will look to make the most of his four games with the White pieces.
Pairings - Round 1: Savian Samuels (USA) vs R Praggnanandhaa (Ind); Javokhir SIndarov (Uzb) vs Levon Aronian (Arm); Vincent Keymer (Ger) vs Wesley So (USA); Fabiano Caruana (USA) vs Jorden Van Foreest (Ned); 8. Anish Giri (Ned) vs Maxime Vachier-Lagrave (Fra).
Published - August 11, 2026 03:02 am IST

stories.headline: India wins 17 medals at U-23 Commonwealth fencing Championship
stories.deck: Team India captured four gold, four silver, and nine bronze medals after the opening day of the event
stories.bodyText:
India secured 17 medals, including four gold at the U-23 Commonwealth Fencing Championship, dominating both the men's and women's individual events currently underway in Lagos, Nigeria.
Team India captured four gold, four silver, and nine bronze medals after the opening day of the event which began on Sunday and will run till August 14.
The national squad displayed absolute dominance across every discipline, ensuring at least one Indian fencer reached the podium in all six individual events spanning Sabre, Foil, and Epee categories, stated a release from the Fencing Association of India.
In the men's Sabre competition, Team India was led by Nikhil Wagh, who secured the gold medal. Lakshay Badser took the silver, while Ashwini Arya and Laishram Moramba shared the Bronze medals to complete a four-way victory.
In the men's Foil, Tejas Patil captured silver and Hemash Sanasam took bronze. In men's Epee, Lokesh Vemani brought home a silver, with Shaurya Ashwini and Godwin Anbkess earning bronze medals.
India's women athletes were equally dominant, securing top honours in two out of three categories.
Joys Ashita won gold in women's Foil ahead of teammate Kanaglakshmi, who earned silver. In women's Epee, Prachi Lohan clinched the gold medal, supported by Nivedhya Nair and Anupriya who both took bronze.
In women's Sabre, Jeferlin claimed gold and Aakhari earned silver, while Shreya Gupta added a bronze medal to round out the women's medal count.
Commending the contingent on their stellar performance, Shri Rajeev Mehta, Secretary General of the Fencing Association of India, stated, "I extend my heartiest congratulations to all our medal winners, coaches, support staff, and families for their relentless dedication and contribution to India's remarkable performance."
Published - August 11, 2026 02:08 am IST

stories.headline: Paris Saint-Germain strengthens defence by signing left back Lucas Digne from Aston Villa
stories.deck: Champions League winner Paris Saint-Germain has strengthened its defense by signing left back Lucas Digne from Aston Villa on a three-year contract
stories.bodyText:
Champions League winner Paris Saint-Germain has strengthened its defense by signing left back Lucas Digne from Aston Villa on a three-year contract.
PSG announced the deal on Sunday evening without giving financial details. Sports daily L'Equipe said it paid the Premier League club €10 million ($11.6 million).
The 33-year-old Digne was born in the Paris suburbs and previously played for PSG after joining from Lille in 2013. He then represented Roma and Barcelona before spending eight years in the Premier League with Everton and Villa.
An energetic defender with accurate passing, the left-footed Digne became a France regular in recent years under former coach Didier Deschamps. He played at the recent World Cup, where Les Bleus reached the semifinals, and has 64 caps.
“I am very honoured to be returning to Paris Saint-Germain following the wonderful experience I had here more than 10 years ago," he said. “I am particularly impressed by how the club has developed over the years.”
PSG recently signed France winger Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco and begins its Ligue 1 title defence at home to Rennes on August 23.
Published - August 11, 2026 01:50 am IST

stories.headline: England, Bayern Munich star Harry Kane set to receive 'Golden Shoe' award
stories.deck: As per the official website of his club Bayern Munich, this is the second time Harry is going to receive the prestigious honour, joining the elite list of players having won it twice, with only legends Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo having won it more
stories.bodyText:
England and Bayern Munich star Harry Kane is set to receive the prestigious ‘Golden Shoe’ honour for emerging as top scorer in European football for the 2025-26 season.
As per the official website of his club Bayern Munich, this is the second time Harry is going to receive the prestigious honour, joining the elite list of players having won it twice, with only legends Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo having won it more. The presentation of the honour will take place on August 19 at the FC Bayern Museum.
The England captain posted 36 Bundesliga goals in another hugely impressive campaign - the same number that earned him the award two years ago. Kane is also seen as one of the leading contenders in this year’s vote for The Best FIFA Men’s Player.
Kane scored a total of 73 goals in 65 competitive appearances for club and country over the past season, as well as setting up eight. With that, he registered the second-highest goal tally in a single season in the 21st century - only Messi (91 goals) in the 2011/12 campaign scored more.
His goals were vital to FC Bayern winning the league, Franz Beckenbauer Supercup and DFB Cup - he netted a hat-trick in the cup final in Berlin and was the top scorer in the competition. The 33-year-old was also crowned Bundesliga top goalscorer for the third year in a row, and finished second in the Champions League scoring chart in 2025/26. Kane is also the fastest player ever to reach 100 goals for a club in one of Europe’s top five leagues.
With the English captaincy armband around his arm, Kane led his country to the FIFA World Cup semifinals this year, their best-ever finish since the 1966 WC triumph. He also became the most prolific British player in the tournament’s history and ended the tournament with seven goals.
Kane is the third Bayern player to be given this prestigious award after Gerd Muller, who won the Golden Shoe in 1970 and 1972, and Robert Lewandowski, who received it in 2021 and 2022 - and he too has now achieved it for the second time.
Herbert Hainer, FC Bayern president said as per a club statement: “Harry Kane stands alongside striking legends like Gerd Muller and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge at FC Bayern - and he has continued this goalscoring legacy into the present by taking the role of the striker to a new level. He is a guiding light to his teams, on and off the pitch, because he always leads with character and a sense of community. We are proud that he’s part of the FC Bayern family.”
Jan-Christian Dreesen, CEO of the club: “When Harry Kane plays, the whole world watches. He has raised FC Bayern and the Bundesliga to a new level. Unusually for a striker, he puts his responsibility to the team above personal success: he’s always thinking about his team-mates, on and off the pitch. His attitude, ability and character make him the most complete striker of his generation - and an absolute role model beyond the field of play. Harry Kane simply has class - and deserves every trophy in the world.”
Max Eberl, Club’s board member for sport, said: “Harry is not just a finisher but a master of the unseen moments, because much of what makes his game so extraordinary are things you do not see: his timing, his awareness of his team-mates and his ability to create space set him apart. His goals are the end product, but beneath them lies a foundation of game intelligence, team spirit and tireless work for the team.
Published - August 11, 2026 01:14 am IST

stories.headline: Barcelona turn down PSG offer for Torres
stories.deck: According to Spanish media reports, Torres, scorer of the winning goal in the 2026 World Cup final, has agreed to join PSG and his former national team coach Luis Enrique
stories.bodyText:
Barcelona on Monday rejected an initial offer from Paris Saint-Germain estimated at €40 million ($46.2 million) for Spanish World Cup winner Ferran Torres, a source within the Catalan club told AFP.
"Negotiations are ongoing" between Barca and PSG, the same source added, confirming reports from the daily Mundo Deportivo.
According to Spanish media reports, Torres, scorer of the winning goal in the 2026 World Cup final, has agreed to join PSG and his former national team coach Luis Enrique.
Out of contract with Barca in June 2027, the 26-year-old forward remained vague about his future in recent interviews he gave during a promotional tour in the United States.
"I have a contract with Barcelona, but in football you never know. I'm just waiting to make the right decision," he said.
When asked if he had a "dream" destination in mind, Torres answered that he did, without revealing it: "I just want to be happy," he replied.
Torres, signed in 2021 from Manchester City for more than 55 million euros, has been used as a centre-forward, backing up Polish striker Robert Lewandowski, since Hansi Flick took over on the Barca bench in the summer of 2024.
Often decisive as a substitute, Torres, who came through Valencia's youth system, has scored 40 goals in 94 matches in all competitions over the last two seasons.
Torres scored Spain's winning goal in extra time of the World Cup final against Argentina last month, giving La Roja their second world title.
Published - August 11, 2026 12:56 am IST
